nodes.author: melisa66413414
nodes.text:
The general shift is significantly more complex than the one-child policy. It’s crucial that we hear from individuals in China who are not government representatives and are free from the fear of Xi. They should be able to access platforms like X without risking their safety or existence just to share the truth. However, that's not possible is it? 
@ChineseEmbinUS @MFA_China 

Per ChatGPT
No, X (formerly known as Twitter) is not accessible in mainland China. The platform has been blocked since 2009 as part of China’s extensive internet censorship system, commonly referred to as the “Great Firewall” .

Despite the ban, some Chinese users access X using Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) or proxy services to bypass these restrictions. However, this practice carries significant risks. Chinese authorities have intensified crackdowns on unauthorized internet use, including the use of VPNs, and have targeted not only content creators but also followers of banned platforms .

Interestingly, while X is banned for the general public, Chinese state media outlets and diplomatic missions maintain official accounts on the platform to disseminate information internationally .

In summary, while technically possible to access X in China through circumvention tools, doing so is illegal and poses considerable risks due to the country’s stringent internet surveillance and censorship policies.
